questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I visited the university a year back, loved campus - it is huge and filled with trees - and learned that USP is a top university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: relatively easy, it is complicated to navigate in the bureaucratic systems of Brazil, but USP was very helpful about it

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received informative e-mails with step by step guides and were invited to a meeting where we were told everything we needed to know

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy and I was lucky to find a nice, cheap and social housing close to campus. I recommend searching in facebook groups such as Repúblicas da USP

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: São Paulo is huge and it can take a long time to get from one place to another. Look for a place to live close to a metro station or close to campus itself. I have been very happy with living in Vila Indiana, you can walk to campus and the neighborhood has a local, studenty feeling to it.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On pós you e-mail a list of the disciplines you want to be enrolled in for the international office along with the name of an adviser (which is very much a formality). They told me that they could enroll me in more courses than I needed too, and then I just had to cancel the ones I wouldn't follow before a certain date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office helped us a lot

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got both of the courses I wanted. Quite a bit were online and therefore unavailable for me, but other than that, I was super successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: talk to other students about there experiences with courses and professors

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: translating master to the Brazilian system is kind of tricky and as a result I ended up having courses on pós-graduação, where people have studies at least five years but some are also writing a PHD. I think a more correct level, and a better academic experience for me would have been taking some classes from the last years of graduação. from what I have heard the courses are excellent and the level is high, and then the chances of socializing a bit should be higher. That being said, my courses on pós were excellent.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was quite similar I would say

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: I can't think of any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think I had a pretty clear idea about the prices, as it is not the first time that I am in São Paulo. But you can eat at the university canteen for 2 reais, which is like 2,50 DKK. That can obviously save you a lot of money. Buying groceries is on the other hand pretty expensive, some things are almost as expensive as in Denmark.

questions.answer: loads and loads. I very much recommend taking advantage of cepeusp, you can participate in all sorts of sports there, and

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: capoeira, football, swimming, yoga. especially capoeira because omowale is a great teacher.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go out, listen to samba, dance forró. go for a hike in parque estadual jaraguá. são paulo is crazy it is good to see something green sometimes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time. São Paulo is super overwhelming especially if you are used to tiny copenhagen, biking everywhere in twenty minutes and never feeling unsafe on the street. I think after a week I relaxed a little bit, and after a month I relaxed a bit more.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join non academic activities, don't be afraid to ask for help

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the unstructuredness of social gatherings is something that I sometimes struggle with. That it is a bit chaotic and can be hard to figure out what you are supposed to do, like what things are rude and such. But what I learned is that the range of acceptable behavior is wider than in Denmark. Not that you can't be rude in Brazil, but I think maybe there is a bigger chance of someone telling you this too.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Brazilians are very generous people. It is very heart warming and charming and beautiful. They will offer you a bite of their cake, a sip of their drink, to come to their birthday, when you have only just met them and so on.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: study Portuguese before you go, stay for two semesters if possible, be curious

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: the semesters starts in the beginning of august and after carnival

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting some very kind, clever and funny people that were so generous as to share their Brazil with me

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Hmm I think it was the way being away from home confronts you with yourself a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
